adrian_b · Nov 28, 2026

"Genetics First" is not an alternative, but an impossibility, so there is no need for anything to be more compelling than it.

"Genetics First" is a pseudo-scientific theory conceived by people who do not understand physics and chemistry, which is equally impossible as the existence of a perpetuum mobile or the like.

By "Genetics First", I mean the use by the first living beings of an information-storage molecule, like the nucleic acids.

Before the first RNA molecule that has ever been synthesized and which stored genetic information, there could not have existed any RNA molecule that had a catalytic a.k.a. enzymatic function.

More precisely, if such an RNA molecule with enzymatic function had existed, it would have disappeared without descendants before the appearance of the first RNA molecule that stored genetic information.

"Storing genetic information" means that the molecule is replicated, so the sequence of its components is copied.

Therefore, the only function of the first RNA molecule that is the ancestor of all nucleic acid molecules was only of storing genetic information, i.e. it was a molecule that was being replicated.

Regardless which are the catalysts used for replication, replication cannot happen for the first time, unless there already exists a process that continuously synthesizes all the required monomers, using energy, which is another way to say that metabolism must already exist.

The synthesis of all the monomers and the extraction from the environment of the energy required for that are much too complicated to happen in a non-living system.

Because the first replicating RNA molecule could not perform any useful function for its host, but its replication consumed monomers like ATP and energy, it was actually a virus.

The same arguments apply even for the improbable case when another molecule capable of storing genetic information had existed before RNA.

Molecules that can store genetic information cannot appear for the first time otherwise than in the form of viruses that are parasites for already existing living systems that have metabolism, i.e. self-reproducing chemical systems that do not use information-storing molecules.

Living beings like us and bacteria, with both metabolism and information-storage molecules, can appear only by the symbiosis between a virus and one of the previous life forms. This matches the fact that the still existing viruses are far more diverse than all the nucleic acids from the genomes of bacteria, archaea and eukaryotes, because all the cellular living beings are descendants of only one of the ancient viruses.

The difference between a self-reproducing chemical system without information-storing molecules and one with information-storing molecules is exactly the same difference as between a hard-wired CPU and a microprogrammed CPU.

The biologists who have conceived the "Genetics First" theory have done this only because due to lack of knowledge about engineering they do not understand the structure of automata and the structural differences between memories and automata (i.e. systems with nested feedback loops of the first order and of the second order).

For a self-reproducing, i.e. living system, there is no need for information storage, but metabolism, i.e. the continuous gathering of energy from the environment and its use to power a cyclical sequence of chemical reactions, is absolutely necessary.

The great advantage brought by memory devices, i.e. macro-molecules that store information, e.g. RNA, is that they have hugely accelerated the rate of evolution, by enabling the exploration of a big space of solutions for improvements, as a consequence of random mutations.

In a self-reproducing chemical system without RNA or the like, evolution can happen only through extremely rare events, because if one of the molecules from the chain of synthesis reactions happens to have a different structure than it should, that most likely will break the reaction chain and that living system will die without descendants.

The use of ATP for energy storage must have preceded by a long time the appearance of the first replicating RNA. The existence of ATP and of its sibling nucleotides lead to side reactions that polymerized them, instead of producing useful molecules, until most likely a self-replicating RNA molecule was synthesized by chance, which then reproduced itself.

In reality, there exists no such thing as a "chicken and egg dilemma". There exists no doubt about which came first, the chicken or the egg. The first chicken must have developed from the first chicken egg. But the first chicken egg must have been produced by something else than a chicken.

That's not all necessarily true

Catalytic RNA has already been demonstrated capable of arusing spontaneously:

"Selective Nonenzymatic Formation of Biologically Common RNA Hairpins (2024)"

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11773311

Also, catalytic RNA does not need to replicate to contribute to abiogenesis

Consider emergence of RNA A which is catalytic but not replicating, producing RNA B which is replicating, and begins copying sequences including the originally non-replicating RNA A

In this scenario, RNA A existed before genetic inheritance emerged, directly facilitated its emergence, and subsequently acquired descendants
